title: Memory leaks and event cleanup
learningObjectives: Explain memory leaks and event cleanup and apply safe browser programming practices.

understand.concept: A memory leak occurs when objects that are no longer needed remain reachable, preventing garbage collection. Common causes include forgotten event listeners, timers, observers, detached DOM references, and long-lived closures. Cleanup removes listeners and cancels work when a component or view is no longer active.
understand.whyItMatters: Leaks can make long-running applications slower and consume memory over time. Lifecycle-aware cleanup is especially important in single-page applications and repeated mount/unmount flows.
understand.analogy: A memory leak is like keeping old equipment in a workspace after the job is finished, leaving less room for current work.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser APIs, security boundaries, and accessibility requirements are defined by web platform standards.

explain.narrative: AbortController can remove listeners registered with its signal, and clearInterval stops the repeating timer. Real components should run cleanup when they are removed.

examples.explanation: AbortController can remove listeners registered with its signal, and clearInterval stops the repeating timer. Real components should run cleanup when they are removed.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates the API or security principle; browser permission or environment support may be required.

practise.guidedTask: Build a component setup function that returns a cleanup function. Remove event listeners, stop timers, and disconnect observers.
practise.independentTask: Build a small browser feature using the API or safety principle. Test normal, denied, unavailable, and invalid cases where relevant.
hints: Treat data from the browser, URL, and network as untrusted.
Ask permission only after explaining the purpose.
Keep sensitive authorization and secrets on a trusted backend.

questions.prompt: Which function stops a repeating timer created by setInterval()?
What is a reliable approach for browser-facing features?
options: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
Assume every browser grants every permission
questions.answer: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
questions.explanation: Browser features should respect user choice, validate inputs, and enforce protected actions on the server.
